title: Private/VPC bootstrap & egress flow: failure scenarios, test matrix, and acceptance contract
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Scope: Define deterministic acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments focused on initial bootstrap (operator/controller startup), controlled egress flows for artifact sync and telemetry, and upgrade/fallback behavior in air-gapped or restricted-egress environments. This doc specifies failure scenarios, observable signals, automated test matrix, and operator playbook required before shipping the private deployment operator 1.0. Goals: (1) ensure zero-surprise bootstraps in customer VPCs with restrictive egress, (2) define minimal egress allowlist and mirror patterns, (3) codify rollback and offline upgrade acceptance criteria for customers running air-gapped clusters.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Operator bootstrap succeeds end-to-end in a VPC with deterministic minimal egress: only HTTPS to allowed mirror endpoints and customer-provided image registry. Full bootstrap means all pods reach Ready and control-plane health checks pass within configured window (15m) without manual operator intervention.

AC-2: When external egress is blocked, operator reports clear, actionable diagnostic codes in /status and logs; each code maps to an automated remediation suggestion in the Console. Example codes: EG-REG-403 (registry auth), EG-DNS-FAIL (DNS resolution), EG-MIRROR-404 (mirror missing artifact).

AC-3: Offline upgrade flow: given a pre-staged image mirror and signed artifacts, the operator can perform a node-by-node upgrade without contacting public endpoints. Acceptance requires a scripted validation run that verifies version skew tolerance and CV health metrics post-upgrade.

AC-4: Controlled egress policy documented and validated: a single-page allowlist with ports/hosts/subnets for (a) artifact mirror, (b) time-limited telemetry relay (optional), (c) license/license-verification endpoints. Tests demonstrate graceful degradation when telemetry is disabled (no crashloops; metrics buffered and exported when connectivity resumes).

AC-5: Rollback contract: if a canary upgrade reduces available replicas below SLO or triggers pod crashloops across dependent services, the operator triggers an automated rollback and generates a postmortem template linking telemetry windows and resource snapshots.

AC-6: Auditability: every bootstrap and upgrade action emits an immutable event with timestamp, operator version, and checksums of pulled images; events are exportable to customer SIEM and visible in Console activity timeline.
AC-7: Test automation: each acceptance criterion is wired to an automated test harness that can run in both the Redwood staging environment and a minimal on-prem emulation (airgapped VM cluster).
test_plan: TP-1: Network partition matrix: simulate blocked egress to registry, partial DNS failure, and intermittent packet loss; verify bootstrap progress and error codes within 15m window.
TP-2: Mirror-first offline install: validate operator install from local mirror with signed manifests; verify checksums and signature verification path.
TP-3: Upgrade smoke: canary subset upgraded while load generators run, monitor P99 latency and replica count; automated rollback if >10% of requests fail at P50 or two or more pods crashloop.
TP-4: Telemetry-disabled validation: run full install with telemetry disabled; ensure metrics are buffered locally and no control-plane features depend on telemetry availability.
TP-5: Deterministic timeout gating: ensure timeouts and retry windows are configurable by customer and defaults are conservative for low-bandwidth environments.
TP-6: Security gate: validate KMS/HSM integration for key rotation during upgrade and that images are validated against signed attestations in offline mode.
rollout_strategy: Staged rollout across customers: 1) internal staging with synthetic VPCs (mirror + restricted egress), 2) opt-in early access customers (two pilot customers with non-production workloads), 3) gated general availability. Rollout toggle controlled by feature flag 'private.egress.validation' and release notes required for pilot customers.
risks: R-1: Customer environments are highly variable; edge cases (proprietary proxies, custom MTU settings) may cause unpredictable bootstrap failures—mitigation: expand test harness with customer-supplied network profiles.
R-2: Mirror freshness and signing mismatch may block upgrades—mitigation: include artifact checksum reconciliation and clear operator UI for manual override with audit log.
R-3: Overly permissive allowlist reduces security posture—mitigation: recommend minimal defaults and provide validated mirror helper tools to seed mirrors securely.
decisions: D-1: Operator will prefer mirror-first fetches with built-in retry/backoff; public endpoints used only as fallback and require explicit operator config.
D-2: Error codes will be standardized across controller components and documented in a single Console help article; each code has a RBAC-visible remediation link.
D-3: We will ship a standalone 'mirror-seeder' CLI to help customers bootstrap mirrors in disconnected environments; the CLI is out-of-band but required for offline acceptance tests.
